Failing which this appeal stands dismissed automatically without further reference to this Bench.
Heard on I. A. No. 02 of 2026, which is an application for exemption from filing the certified copy of the order passed under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
On due consideration, the application I. A. No. 02 of 2026 is allowed.
Also heard on I. A. No. 01 of 2026, which is an application for grant of stay.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that without there being any cogent and prudent evidence available on record the learned Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.
36,000/-pm.
She further submits that although an income tax return was filed, no evidence regarding the source of such income was produced before the Claims Tribunal.
Therefore, the learned Tribunal has awarded an excessive and exaggerated amount of compensation.

After hearing learned counsel for the appellant, it is ordered that on appellant's depositing 75% of the awarded amount alongwith the interest before the Claims Tribunal AMITA within a period of 45 days from today, recovery of remainder DUBEY shall remain stayed against the appellant.
The respondents/claimants are at liberty to withdraw Date:
